body.statement:
For every sequence of even horizons \(T\to\infty\) and capacities \(B_T\ge 1\),
\[
R_T(B_T)\to 0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad B_T\to\infty.
\]
By Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:causal\text{-}regret\text{-}reduction}\) and Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:offline\text{-}adjacent}\), the condition on the left is exactly uniform-minimax ex ante conditional design-variance equivalence to the full-information adjacent-\(g\) prognostic oracle (the Bai oracle): its additive variance excess is \(o(T^{-1})\). This is an additive uniform-minimax statement only; it does not assert relative precision, a central limit theorem, feasible inference, or necessity under each fixed law.
body.justification: The iff statement identifies the exact memory-growth requirement for offline first-order precision.
body.gap: Morrison gives one sufficient growing-reservoir schedule; necessity and the equivalence for arbitrary hard-cap schedules are not published.
body.consumer: An experimenter can determine whether a proposed reservoir growth plan is asymptotically adequate without knowing \(g\).
body.proof_tex:
For a policy \(\pi\in\Pi_{T,B}\) and a law \(P\in\mathcal P_{\beta,d}(L,G,H,\underline f,\overline f)\), set
\[
V_\pi(W,\xi)
=\operatorname{Var}_Z\!\left\{
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{IPW}}(M_\pi)
\,\middle|\,(W_i)_{i=1}^T,\xi
\right\}
\]
and, for \(M\in\mathfrak M_T\), set
\[
V_M(W)
=\operatorname{Var}_Z\!\left\{
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{IPW}}(M)
\,\middle|\,(W_i)_{i=1}^T
\right\}.
\]
Define the uniform-minimax ex ante mean conditional design-variance excess by
\[
\Delta_T(B)
=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi_{T,B}}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\beta,d}(L,G,H,\underline f,\overline f)}
\mathbb E_{P,\xi}\!\left[
\mathbb E_P\!\left\{V_\pi(W,\xi)\,\middle|\,(X_i)_{i=1}^T,\xi\right\}
-\min_{M\in\mathfrak M_T}
\mathbb E_P\!\left\{V_M(W)\,\middle|\,(X_i)_{i=1}^T\right\}
\right].
\]
Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:causal\text{-}regret\text{-}reduction}\), applied for each admissible pair \((\pi,P)\), and Definition \(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}regret}\) give the exact equality
\[
R_T(B)=T\Delta_T(B).
\tag{1}
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:offline\text{-}adjacent}\) identifies the full-information prognostic oracle appearing in \(\Delta_T(B)\): after sorting the realized values \(g(X_i)\), it pairs consecutive order statistics. Thus it is the adjacent-\(g\) oracle used as the Bai prognostic benchmark. In particular, (1) proves
\[
R_T(B_T)\to0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Delta_T(B_T)=o(T^{-1}).
\tag{2}
\]
This establishes the claimed additive variance interpretation without dividing by the oracle variance and without invoking a limit distribution or a variance estimator.

It remains to characterize when \(R_T(B_T)\to0\). Write
\[
b_T=\min\{B_T,T/2\}.
\]
The exponent \(\alpha=2\beta/d\) is strictly positive because \(\beta>0\) and \(d\ge1\). Suppose first that \(B_T\to\infty\). Since also \(T/2\to\infty\), we have \(b_T\to\infty\). Choose the integer
\[
m_T=\min\{b_T,\lfloor T^{1/2}\rfloor\}.
\]
For all sufficiently large even \(T\), \(1\le m_T\le b_T\), while \(m_T\to\infty\) and
\[
0\le \frac{m_T}{T}\le T^{-1/2}\to0.
\]
The implementable design supplied by Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:capped\text{-}grid\text{-}upper}\) is therefore feasible at capacity \(B_T\), and its bound yields
\[
0\le R_T(B_T)
\le C\left\{m_T^{-\alpha}+\frac{m_T}{T}\right\}
\longrightarrow0,
\tag{3}
\]
because \(m_T\to\infty\) and \(\alpha>0\).

Conversely, suppose that \(B_T\not\to\infty\). By the definition of divergence to infinity, there exist an integer \(K\ge1\) and an infinite subsequence of even horizons, again denoted by \(T\), on which \(B_T\le K\). On that subsequence, \(1\le b_T\le K\). Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:all\text{-}policy\text{-}lower\text{-}frontier}\) and Definition \(\mathrm{def:frontier}\) imply
\[
R_T(B_T)
\ge cF_\alpha(T,b_T)
=c\left\{b_T^{-\alpha}+\frac1T\sum_{r=1}^{b_T}r^{-\alpha}\right\}
\ge cb_T^{-\alpha}
\ge cK^{-\alpha}>0.
\tag{4}
\]
Hence \(R_T(B_T)\) cannot converge to zero. Equations (3) and (4) prove
\[
R_T(B_T)\to0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad B_T\to\infty,
\]
and combining this equivalence with (2) proves the stated uniform-minimax ex ante additive \(o(T^{-1})\) design-variance equivalence. The subsequence argument is minimax over the stated law class and therefore makes no per-law necessity claim.
